title: Madhubala's birth chart
metaDescription: Madhubala's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 25.1° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: Venus and Saturn within 0.7°, taste wired to structure. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 25.1° Aquarius — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Venus. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aquarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Venus at 8.5° Aquarius, Mars at 16.5° Virgo. Venus in a air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a earth sign reads as drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Pluto — a sextile holding at 0.5°. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Venus conjunction Saturn at 0.7°, and Uranus square Pluto at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aquarius at 25.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Virgo at 21.2° is in detriment; Saturn in Aquarius at 9.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, earth 3, fire 1, water 1 across the elements, and fixed 3, cardinal 3, mutable 3 across the modalities. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. Mercury crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day, so its sign is left open. Mars, Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 11.8°.
